c.pop: ~29,000 (Murree town; the wider hill station district sees far more visitors)
c.tagline: A colonial-era hill station in the pines, Pakistan's classic escape from the summer plains
langs: English (widely spoken, colonial-era hill station heritage)

card: Cards are accepted at larger hotels but most Mall Road shops, restaurants, and chairlifts are cash-only. ATMs are available on Mall Road and in the Kashmir Point area.

taxi.color: no standard livery — mostly private sedans
taxi.fareNote: Fares are negotiated; expect heavy traffic and surge pricing on Mall Road during peak summer weekends

emergency.note: Serious cases are often transferred to Rawalpindi or Islamabad, about 1.5-2 hours away depending on traffic

religion: small Christian minority (a legacy of the colonial-era hill station and its churches)
walk: Mall Road and the town center are walkable (and pedestrian-only during peak season), with Kashmir Point and Pindi Point reachable on foot or a short taxi ride; Patriata and Ayubia require a car or taxi.

safety.safety: Very safe and family-friendly; Murree is Pakistan's most visited hill station and well set up for tourists
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; the main practical concerns are heavy traffic congestion and crowd crush on Mall Road during peak summer weekends and winter snowfall

hood_landmark.Kashmir Point: Kashmir Point viewpoint over the valley
hood_landmark.Jhika Gali: Jhika Gali's pine-forest hotels and quieter pace

avoid.reason: Mall Road gets crushingly crowded on peak weekends with pickpocketing and staring/harassment of women, and winter snowstorms can strand traffic on the access roads.

hood_desc: The bustling colonial-era heart of Murree, lined with shops, cafes, and the historic Holy Trinity Church — the busiest and most central base.
A scenic residential ridge east of Mall Road with panoramic valley views and several mid-range hotels.
A quieter viewpoint area with a chairlift down into the valley, popular for sunset views away from Mall Road's crowds.
A pine-forested stretch a short drive from central Murree, favored for its cooler, calmer atmosphere and family resorts.
A separate hill station about 45 minutes from Murree proper, known for its cable car and chairlift over forested slopes — a popular day-trip extension.

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; tap water is unreliable.

transit.sys: No formal public transit; local taxis and shared vans cover the town and connections to Rawalpindi/Islamabad
transit.pay: Cash (PKR), fare per seat or negotiated
transit.note: Mall Road becomes pedestrian-only during peak evening hours in summer; most visitors walk the promenade and taxi to outlying viewpoints

transport.air: Nearest airport is Islamabad International (ISB), about 60 km / 1.5-2 hours by road
transport.train: No rail service to Murree; the nearest station is in Rawalpindi
transport.bus: Frequent vans and coaches connect Murree to Rawalpindi and Islamabad (about 1.5-2 hours)
transport.ferry: None — Murree is an inland hill station with no ferry service
transport.car: Reachable via the Islamabad Expressway and Murree Road; expect heavy traffic and slow going on weekends and in winter snow

net.m: Good 4G coverage from Jazz, Zong, Telenor, and Ufone in Murree town; signal can weaken in surrounding forested areas
net.w: Wifi is available in most hotels and cafes on Mall Road
net.gb: ~$2-5 for a prepaid SIM with a few GB
net.fwn: Some social media and VOIP services face intermittent restrictions in Pakistan; a VPN can help but isn't always necessary
net.ap: A local Jazz or Zong SIM is easy to buy in Islamabad or Rawalpindi with your passport before heading up to Murree

tip.s: Tipping (rounding up) is appreciated for hotel staff and drivers
tip.r: 10% is welcomed at restaurants, though not obligatory
